# garrytan/gstack-evals#141: native adversarial findings #4 and #6, head a752186 (tree 0ac70e872724875710ccc47f9c93b7b30a58604a)
Copied verbatim from /home/user/.capy/work/ship-141/run/p2/out/adversarial-native.txt

4. **driver.ts:352, 561 and 618 (the C1 ruling): skill-eval sessions now end with background Agents still running and leave no structured record.** run-host.ts:352 passes no wait. Claude Code 2.1.314 runs Agent calls in the background by default. So a skill-eval `--host claude` session ends and is graded on its "agents launched, waiting" turn, which is the original GST-734 bug. Its record also has no `session_end`, only a line in cli-stderr.log. The CREW rule asks for a per-arm count of sessions that ended with tasks pending, and these records can't give that count. Grades for skills that hand work to Agents may be deflated with nothing marking them. Old cached sessions do not mix in, because adapterSha256 hashes driver.ts. The fix: keep emitting `session_end` (cause `tasks_pending`, `waited_ms` 0) when no wait is set, and leave the hold opt-in. That reverses the C1 test's `"session_end" in r.outcome === false` assertion, so the C1 owner needs to agree. FIXABLE. Severity: Medium. Blocks: no

6. **driver.ts:404-407: the timeout branch for an idle session sets `overdue = true` without checking `stop`.** Here is the case. A background agent's refused request sets a stop while the main agent is idle, such as `cap_stop`, or an infra failure does. The timer then fires during abort teardown. The record ends up with a `cap_stop` or infra termination but `session_end.cause` "deadline". The `watch` interval already checks `stop`. Fix: `else if (idleSince !== null && !stop)`. FIXABLE. Severity: Low. Blocks: no
